question: What does the per-party check cost in the circuit, end to end?
openings_arithmetic: At the 6-bit coefficients the generator emits, one combination binds a party at about 2^-6, so 7 repetitions give 2^-42 --- per party. That is repeats x n = 49 openings against the aggregate check's 7. They are all independent, so they cost ONE round together, which is why the round count does not move.

predictions.traffic about 3 kB more, +0.02 percent: PARTLY WRONG. Measured 28.3 kB, +0.068 percent. The estimate assumed 7 openings; at 6-bit coefficients it is 49, because soundness per party has to be bought by repetition the same way the aggregate check buys it. The conclusion --- negligible --- survives; the number was 10x light.
predictions.the combination itself is free: holds: public coefficient times secret share is local, and only the openings travel

what_is_now_complete: The dealer publishes share commitments (already did). The circuit folds each share into its own node's accumulator as it is read and opens one value per node per repetition. zk/input_check.py verify_per_party recomputes the coefficients from the published commitments and checks each opening. A failing one names a node, to anybody.
what_is_still_not: Naming is not preventing and not repairing. By the time the openings are checked the circuit has computed on the substituted input. Rung 4, not rung 5.
